children: Bitcoin holders on Sui can now put their coins to work without handing them to a single custodian. Hashi, the network's Bitcoin finance protocol, is live on mainnet, and its hBTC token can be used as collateral in lending and other onchain products.
Users deposit BTC, which stays on the Bitcoin network, and Hashi mints hBTC on Sui at a 1:1 ratio, according to a statement Sui shared with The Block.

Sui said Hashi is decentralized by design, with security handled by the network's validators rather than one company. Hashi uses Sui validators alongside a 2-of-2 multisig arrangement, meaning two separate signatures are required before any funds can move. The stated aim is that no central party controls deposits.
Deposits also require six Bitcoin confirmations before hBTC is minted.

Hashi went live on mainnet on November 13, 2026, with Sui's official announcement following on November 19. That staggered rollout gave the protocol about a week of quiet operation before the spotlight arrived.
At launch, Hashi reported roughly 14.43 BTC in reserves, worth approximately $994,000.
Over 20 partners committed more than $500 million in capital to support Hashi, a pledge announced on October 8, 2026.
The first concrete use case is lending through Fluid, which accepts hBTC as collateral for USDC loans. Partners also plan to roll out vault and lending products.
Anchorage Digital and Fluid have both aligned with Hashi.

For Bitcoin holders, the appeal is straightforward. They can borrow USDC against their BTC through Fluid while keeping exposure to Bitcoin itself. The trade-off is taking on smart contract risk, liquidation risk if prices move sharply, and reliance on a custody model that is brand new on mainnet.
The 2-of-2 multisig setup protects against one party acting alone. It also means both parties must be available and functioning for withdrawals to proceed.
Anchorage Digital's involvement and the more than $500 million in partner commitments suggest Hashi is aiming beyond retail users.

The key metric going forward is reserve growth. Hashi launched with roughly 14.43 BTC backing its supply. Also worth tracking: the rollout of the partner vault and lending products, and whether additional protocols beyond Fluid begin accepting hBTC as collateral.

title: Hashi goes live on Sui mainnet, turning Bitcoin into lending collateral
